acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

applyProductionExclusion(address).details: REFUSES (returns false, does not revert) when the visible pool would not survive      the exclusion. Selection takes `min(cap, visible)` with no backfill floor, so      excluding the marginal candidate shrinks the committee — the opposite of what the      tier exists to do. The pool is counted at the epoch the stamp will BITE from      (`_currentEpoch() + 1`), against that epoch's cap.      Returning `false` rather than reverting is load-bearing: the caller must be able      to leave NO trace of a refused stamp — no ladder increment, no pending entry —      and a revert inside the close's fail-loud leg would halt the chain over a      condition that is a normal, expected outcome on a small network.      Best-effort, never a guarantee: the stamp bites two selection epochs after this      check, and registrations in between can invalidate it either way.

commitEpochCommittee(address[]).details: System call: the sequencer injects this once on the first block of      a new epoch (zero gas price, from coinbase), passing the SAME      ordered committee it feeds Commonware `Oracle::track`. The contract      does NOT trust that input: it verifies `committee` is exactly the      keyed subset of `_getValidators()` top-k, strictly ascending by      `peerPubkey` (the unique canonical Simplex committee order). The sequencer      has zero freedom — it can only submit the one array the contract      would itself derive; off-chain sorting just saves the O(m^2)      on-chain sort. Idempotent + strictly monotonic — a re-call for an      already/older epoch is a no-op; a missed epoch has no record (its      evidence is unslashable, by design).

params.committee: Validators in ascending-`peerPubkey` order. Reverts        unless it equals the keyed top-k set exactly.

getEpochCommitteeLength(uint64).details: A single SLOAD — avoids copying the whole committee array to memory      just to read its length (the per-block `processBitmap` hot path).

getEpochCommitteeWithStakes(uint64).details: `stakes[i]` is full-precision wei (`totalDelegatedToValidatorAt`, the      at-or-before-`epoch` snapshot — the same source committee selection      ranks by, never the validator's unclamped latest `changedAt` read).

getValidatorDelegatedStakeAt(address,uin.details: Uses the REBASED epoch (`dposActivationBlock`-relative, matching      {currentEpoch}) and the at-or-before snapshot — the same effective-stake      source committee selection ranks by. This is the canonical governance      voting-power read; it does not leak the validator's latest `changedAt`      snapshot for empty epochs, so a past `blockNumber` resolves to the stake      actually effective then rather than the validator's latest stake.

params.commissionRate: The commission rate of the validators.
params.initialOwner: The address of the initial owner of the staking contract.
params.initialStakes: The initial stakes of the validators.
params.validators: The addresses of initial validators to be added to the staking contract.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

releaseProductionExclusion(address).details: Re-stamps ONLY for a validator that is still Active and not tombstoned. The      visibility stamp is last-write-wins with a single pending transition and the      selection filter is the stamp and nothing else — with deliberately no live      tombstone check — so a blind re-stamp here would permanently re-seat a slashed,      tombstoned equivocator.      The caller clears its own record either way. That is not laxity: leaving a      released-but-not-restamped entry pending would pin a slot in the `<= f`      concurrent-exclusion budget forever. If the validator becomes Active again later,      governance activation re-stamps visibility on its own path.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

params.blsPoPUncompressed: 128 B EIP-2537 G1 PoP signature — verify-only.
params.blsPubkeyUncompressed: 256 B EIP-2537 G2 — compressed on-chain                              to the stored 96 B identity.

settleEpochStipendFrom(uint64).details: The tolerant leg of the close: the caller wraps this in a gas-bounded `try` and      swallows a failure, so a transient settle failure delays payment by one epoch and      a deterministic one freezes the stipend cursor loudly — neither touches chain      liveness. The cursor advances only past an actually-settled epoch, so the retry is      contiguous.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner.

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`, and subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

applyProductionExclusion(address).notice: Stamp `validatorAddress` selection-invisible for a production-liveness         exclusion. Returns whether the stamp was actually written.

commitEpochCommittee(address[]).notice: Freezes the canonical consensus committee for the current epoch.

committeeSelectionEpoch().notice: The epoch whose EffBal selects the next committee to commit:         `nextEpochToCommit() - 2` (clamped to 0 at genesis). The executor         passes this to getValidatorsWithKeysAt so the derived committee         matches the contract's `_getValidatorsAt(selectionEpoch)` verify.         2-epoch warm-up: committee[target] is selected from EffBal(target-2)         and committed a full epoch before its DKG (which runs in target-1),         so the DKG deals over an already-frozen roster.

currentEpoch().notice: Returns the epoch derived from the current block number.

disableValidator(address).notice: Disables a validator without deleting its historical state.

getDkgQual(uint64).notice: Whether a committee MINT (a genuine membership change vs the incumbent,         so a fresh beacon key is dealt in the DKG) was recorded for `epoch`.         Set DETERMINISTICALLY at commit time by {StakingDpos.commitEpochCommittee}         (`committee[epoch] != committee[epoch-1]`) — the consensus beacon-key         carry arbiter reads it to find the newest key epoch. Replaces the former         permissionless `recordDkgQual` marker.

getEpochCommittee(uint64).notice: Returns the frozen committee for `epoch` (Simplex committee order), or         empty if never committed. Consumed by fluent-staking-reader.

getEpochCommitteeLength(uint64).notice: Length of the frozen committee for `epoch` (0 if uncommitted).

getEpochCommitteeWithStakes(uint64).notice: Frozen committee for `epoch` (Simplex order) with each member's keys         and frozen effective stake (wei). One atomic per-epoch snapshot read         for stake-weighted leader election. Empty arrays if uncommitted.

getEpochRewards(uint64).notice: Total BLEND reward credited across `epoch`'s committee, summed for an off-chain APR         basis. Read-only.

getRegistryWithKeys().notice: The FULL Active-status validator registry (`_activeValidatorsList`)         with consensus keys — unlike {getValidatorsWithKeys}, NOT truncated         to the stake-weighted top-k committee. Feeds the consensus p2p         tier-2 peer set: every activated validator (in or out of the         committee, including the sequencer) stays connected.

getValidatorByOwner(address).notice: Returns the validator address owned by `owner`, or zero when none is registered.

getValidatorDelegatedStakeAt(address,uin.notice: Returns `validator`'s effective delegated stake (voting power) as of `blockNumber`.

getValidatorStatus(address).notice: Returns current validator metadata and latest accounting snapshot.

getValidators().notice: Returns the current active validator set ordered by delegated amount.

getValidatorsWithKeys().notice: Returns active validators with their consensus keys in a single call.

getValidatorsWithKeysAt(uint64).notice: Epoch-parameterized variant of getValidatorsWithKeys: the         stake-weighted keyed top-k set as of `epoch`. The executor uses         this to derive the committee for a future epoch it is about to         commit one epoch ahead (see commitEpochCommittee).

isValidator(address).notice: Returns whether `validator` is known to the staking contract in any status.

isValidatorActive(address).notice: Returns whether `validator` is currently in the active validator set.

nextEpochToCommit().notice: The next epoch whose committee is not yet committed         (== lastCommittedEpochP1). The executor reads this to know which         epoch to derive + commit next in its ahead-of-time catch-up loop.

registerValidator(address,uint16,uint256.notice: Registers `validator` with `msg.sender` as owner and an initial self-stake.

releaseProductionExclusion(address).notice: Restore selection visibility at the end of a production-liveness exclusion.

resolveSigner(uint64,uint32).notice: Resolves a Simplex signer index for a past epoch to the         validator address, using that epoch's frozen committee.

setConsensusKeys(address,bytes,bytes,byt.notice: Register consensus keys for `validator` with on-chain         Proof-of-Possession. One-shot — no rotation in v1.

settleEpochStipendFrom(uint64).notice: Settle the per-epoch BLEND stipend, driven by the liveness predeploy's epoch         close instead of its own system call.

documentation.text:
Here is min/max commission rates. Lets don't allow to set more than 30% of validator commission, because it's
 too big commission for validator. Commission rate is a percents divided by 100 stored with 0 decimals as percents*100 (=pc/1e2*1e4)
 Here is some examples:
 + 0.3% => 0.3*100=30
 + 3% => 3*100=300
 + 30% => 30*100=3000

@notice BlendReserve predeploy address — the stipend source `settleEpochStipendFrom` draws from.
         Private immutable here (not a ChainConfig field) to avoid a cross-repo ABI break.

@dev Gates the `ProductionLiveness` predeploy as the sole caller of the stipend
      settle and both exclusion stamps. These are INTERNAL contract calls made from
      inside the predeploy's epoch close, not executor syscalls, so `onlySystemCall`
      would reject all three — `msg.sender` is the predeploy, not the system sentinel.

documentation.text:
@dev Rebased epoch at an arbitrary block. DPoS epochs are numbered relative to
      `dposActivationBlock` so a Tempo→DPoS migration anchor at a high block becomes
      epoch 0 (see ChainConfig.dposActivationBlock). Pre-activation blocks clamp to 0 —
      reachable only in a predeploy window before the switch; in production the
      contract is introduced at activation so block.number >= activation always holds.
      activation == 0 ⇒ absolute numbering (degenerate). Single source of the
      block→epoch formula: shared by `_currentEpoch` and the block-parameterized
      voting-power read (`getValidatorDelegatedStakeAt`) so governance and staking can
      never disagree on epoch numbering (audit 2b).
